source.title: Few-Shot Truly Benign DPO Attack for Jailbreaking LLMs
source.authors: Sangyeon Yoon; Wonje Jeung; Yoonjun Cho; Dongjae Jeon; Albert No

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance, using DPO preference tuning rather than the original SFT method.
record.gate_note: The paper cites harmful fine-tuning and first-token-depth work, but reports no new harmful-example fine-tuning, aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement, compliant-opening prefill test, adversarial-suffix test, or decoding-change test. Its discussion of an aligned-model prefix defense reports no result for that defense. The reported preference-data detection rates and downstream capability scores do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures harmful-prompt ASR after DPO fine-tuning on benign preference pairs (helpful answer preferred over refusal). This is a different training method aimed at V2's question: does benign fine-tuning raise harmful compliance? It tests four OpenAI models and several Llama/Qwen models against base-model ASR.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors also stress that the data evades moderation and frontier-LLM auditors, and that the effect persists under LoRA and with one pair on open-weight models.
record.recipe_differences: This paper tests benign DPO preference tuning, not the original harmful-example SFT method or the first-token-depth method. Its training pairs prefer a normal helpful answer to a refusal on benign prompts.
record.method_sensitivity: ASR varies with the dispreferred response construction: using a non-refusal output weakens the attack, while 10 refusal variants increase it. Preferred-response construction also changes ASR modestly. The paper reports results across several benchmarks, models, training sample counts, and full versus LoRA fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: During DPO on Llama-3.1 8B, the cross-entropy loss of refusals to unseen harmful queries rises together with the dispreferred-refusal loss. A gradient-similarity analysis over the first 10 response tokens shows DPO gradients align with answering harmful prompts (0.158) and against refusing them (−0.135); SFT gradients from the Indirect attack show 0.072 and 0.009.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preference objectives that penalize refusal on benign prompts suppress a shared refusal direction that generalizes to harmful prompts, more strongly than SFT.

record.problems: Several relevant results are presented only as figures without numerical values in the text. The main ASR evaluation uses GPT-5-mini as judge, though the paper reports pairwise agreement with two human annotators on a balanced subset. The open-weight main results and low-data trajectories are not numerically specified in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Downstream capability scores, detectability rates, judge-validation agreement, and gradient-similarity values were not included because they do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: Ordinary benign SFT data and other preference objectives (only DPO with β=0.1 is tested). Models larger than 8B among open weights.

missing.what: Base-model ASR implied by the reported multipliers (GPT-4o 4.96×, GPT-4.1 10.64×, mini 5.59×, nano 13.78×); needed as baselines for r1–r4

Downstream capability after the attack: GSM8k is similar to or above base, while IFEval drops somewhat (e.g. GPT-4o 91.13→82.25). This bears on whether the erosion is selective rather than general damage.

record.verdict_notes: The main preferred responses were generated with the elicitation suffix 'Sure, there's the method to', so they open compliantly, similar to the Indirect attack. The vanilla-aligned variant (r13, r14) removes this suffix and remains effective, so the result does not hinge on it. The judge is GPT-5-mini, which agreed with each human annotator about 82% of the time (humans agreed with each other 76%). The study is not an original source. Rows r9–r11 and r13 were moved from limits_scope to supports, since their ASR stays high.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not fine-tune on harmful examples; harmful-example results are cited from prior work.
Tests benign DPO preference data, including an over-refusal-reduction setting; does not test ordinary benign SFT data or other preference objectives.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models.
No test of compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
The LoRA experiment tests vulnerability under parameter-efficient fine-tuning, not whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
The paper analyzes DPO refusal suppression and gradient similarity, but does not test why safety is shallow or measure response-position depth.
No training intended to spread safety across response positions or evaluation of whether such deepening holds up.

conditions.value: 250 safe XSTEST prompts incorrectly refused by the base model

relationships.condition: Benign DPO with refusal as the dispreferred response, on GPT-4o/4.1/4.1-mini/4.1-nano and Llama/Qwen 1B–8B; across refusal templates, preferred-response constructions, 1–10 samples, LoRA or full fine-tuning, five benchmarks, and the realistic XSTest over-refusal setting
relationships.reason: ASR rises 5–14× over base on OpenAI models (r1–r4). Alternative refusal templates and vanilla preferred answers stay high (r9–r11, r13, r14). The XSTest setting goes 11.33%→87.33% (r30). Other rows are figure-only or table values (r5–r8, r15–r29).
relationships.display_finding: Attack success rose 5–14 times over base on OpenAI models, stayed high with other refusal templates and plain preferred answers, and went from 11.33% to 87.33% in the XSTest over-refusal setting.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Benign DPO with refusal as the dispreferred response, on GPT-4o/4.1/4.1-mini/4.1-nano and Llama/Qwen 1B–8B; across refusal templates, preferred-response constructions, 1–10 samples, LoRA or full fine-tuning, five benchmarks, and the realistic XSTest over-refusal setting
labels.reason: Sections 5.2–5.7 report increased harmful compliance across these tested settings. The OpenAI increases are 4.96–13.78× base; Table 4 reports Llama-3.1 8B ASR increasing from 11.33% to 87.33%.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: GPT-4o, dispreferred response replaced by a non-refusal output
labels.reason: Table 1 reports 21.00% ± 0.91 versus 59.13% ± 1.24 with refusal dispreferred. This supports dependence of effect magnitude on the dispreferred response, not complete dependence of safety erosion on refusals.

relation.reason: The study directly measures harmful-response ASR after benign DPO and compares it with base models and alternative training constructions.

tranche.reason: DPO on benign preference pairs is a different training method testing whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance.

source_check.notes: For r1–r4, numeric untreated baselines are not explicitly stated; dividing ASRs by the reported rounded multipliers yields estimates, not directly reported baseline cells. The r12 comparator is correctly identified as another post-training condition.

statements.correction: Table 1: GPT-4o refusal-dispreferred ASR = 59.13% ± 1.24; non-refusal-dispreferred ASR = 21.00% ± 0.91. Section 5.3: replacing refusal substantially weakens the attack. These are alternative post-training conditions; verdict = limits_scope.
statements.problem: The numerical comparison is correct, but challenges is too strong for this study: weaker harmful compliance under an alternative construction does not establish an absent or reversed V2 effect.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: DPO fine-tuning with benign preference data on tested proprietary and open-weight models, and the XSTEST over-refusal-reduction setting
reader_labels.reason: Harmful-response ASR is high after benign DPO training, including 59.13% on GPT-4o, 70.20% on GPT-4.1, and 87.33% after the XSTEST-based Llama-3.1 8B fine-tuning; see r1–r8 and r30.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Alternative DPO pair construction on GPT-4o
reader_labels.reason: The effect depends in part on the construction: a non-refusal dispreferred output yields 21.00 ± 0.91 ASR, substantially below the refusal-based conditions, while alternative refusal templates retain high ASR; see r9–r13.
